concept.name: Primary peg order
concept.definition: A pegged order whose working price tracks the same side of the market: a buy primary peg follows the national best bid, a sell primary peg follows the national best offer, usually plus or minus an offset. It keeps the order at the top of its side's queue without crossing the spread.
concept.intuition: It is 'stay on the bid (or offer) automatically' - you remain competitively posted as a liquidity provider while the market moves.
concept.mechanics: The venue re-prices the order as the same-side NBBO quote moves (Cboe ExecInst R: peg Buy to NBB, Sell to NBO), with an optional offset to be more or less aggressive, subject to a cap limit. The order adds liquidity and, being displayed or non-displayed per instructions, earns maker treatment on execution.
concept.formula: Buy working price = national best bid + offset; sell working price = national best offer - offset (bounded by the cap limit price).
concept.failure_modes: Because it only ever posts passively, a primary peg can go unfilled for an entire move; and when it does fill, it is often because a more aggressive trader expects the quote to move through it (adverse selection).
concept.misconceptions: Primary peg is not a market order with a floating cap - it never takes liquidity. It also does not follow the trader's own venue quote but the national same-side best quote.
concept.example: With NBBO at $30.00 x $30.02, your primary-pegged buy sits at $30.00; when the bid steps to $30.01, your order re-prices to $30.01 automatically.

citations.source: Cboe Titanium U.S. Equities BOE Specification
citations.section: ExecInst R = Primary Peg (peg Buy to NBB, Sell to NBO)
